Location: Jl. Raya Ubud, Ubud, Gianyar, Bali
 Opening Hours: 08:00 AM – 06:00 PM (some stalls open earlier)
 Ubud Art Market Entrance Fee: Free
 Best Time to Visit: 08:00 – 10:00 AM Average Visit Duration: 1–2 hours

The Ubud Art Market is located in the center of Ubud, directly across from Ubud Palace and within walking distance of Saraswati Temple. It is one of the most popular traditional markets in Ubud for buying souvenirs and handmade Balinese crafts. [...] ## Best Time to Visit Ubud Art Market

Choosing the right time makes a big difference in your shopping experience.

Morning (08:00 – 10:00 AM) – BEST TIME

 Less crowded
 Cooler weather
 Better bargaining opportunities
 Sellers more open to negotiation

Morning is highly recommended if you want a relaxed shopping experience.

Afternoon (10:00 AM – 03:00 PM)

 Peak hours
 More tourists
 Harder to bargain
 Parking becomes limited [...] The market is open daily from 08:00 to 18:00, and some of the stalls are even open until late at night. The market is divided into two main allotments. The western block is the main art market, and the eastern block is a traditional market serving daily groceries and necessities.

results.title: Ubud Market — Ubud, Indonesia
results.content: This traditional indoor and outdoor market in the center of Ubud is actually two markets — one for tourists and another for locals. It’s held daily in a two- story building and on the streets across from the Puri Saren Royal Ubud Palace from around 4 AM until 6 PM. The market was made famous by the movie Eat Pray Love, but it has been a busy spot for generations. You’ll find everything from produce to artwork to t-shirts. Located in central Bali in the Gianyar Province, Ubud is the center of [...] The Ubud Art Market, or Pasar Seni Ubud, begins on the Western side around 6 AM. You’ll find local craftsmen and artists hawking masks, statues, traditional batik, baskets, bags, and other handmade goods. Most of these goods are made in the neighboring villages. Ubud’s royalty has a long tradition as patrons of local artisans, which is why the market is located across the street from the Royal Palace. There’s also plenty of tourist trinkets, such as t-shirts, hats, and bracelets. [...] up quickly by restaurateurs and families. By about 9 AM, the traditional market is packing up, and more tourist-oriented items begin to appear in the stalls.
